title: Anti-Kuomintang Coalition
capsule: The Anti-Kuomintang Coalition, known primarily as the Central Plains War (中原大戰), was a military alliance of dissident Nationalist warlords — chiefly Feng Yuxiang, Yan Xishan, and the Guangxi Clique under Li Zongren — who united in 1930 to challenge Chiang Kai-shek's Nanjing government. Fighting from May to November 1930 across the Central Plain involved over a million troops and produced roughly 300,000 casualties, making it the largest battle of the warlord era. The coalition collapsed when Zhang Xueliang's Manchurian forces declared for Chiang in September 1930, leaving the Nanjing government as the dominant Chinese authority until the Japanese invasion deepened after 1931.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The coalition's territorial control is poorly defined geographically — it constituted overlapping military zones rather than a coherent administrative entity — making precise boundary attestation impossible.
